questions: How many crystals did you measure by transport and how many cleaves, tips and areas by STM, and how many of these showed the two-gap spectrum on the 1H termination?
Why were the others set aside, if any were?
Which ranges did you measure beyond the ones shown, in particular a temperature series of the 1H spectrum between 0.3 K and Tc, fields between 0 and 1 kG, and spectra on other 1H areas?

What does the second-best dataset look like? The zero-field 1H spectrum in Supp. Fig. 4b seems, by my reading, to have coherence peaks nearer ±0.45 mV than the ±0.53 mV of Fig. 4a; does it show the 300 µeV kink, and what differs between the two (tip, area, cooldown, setpoint)?

What are the fitted weights N1 and N2, the effective temperature and the lock-in modulation for Fig. 4a, and how much do Δ2 and the fit quality change if the broadening is fixed at the value that fits the SnS spectrum? The single-gap fit in Supp. Fig. 2 needed an effective temperature of 900 mK.
Since the SnS gap (440 µeV) sits between your two 1H gaps, have you fit the 1H and SnS spectra together with a coupled-layer McMillan model, and what interlayer coupling does such a fit allow?

Can you place each gap on a Fermi pocket, for example with quasiparticle interference or the field dependence of each d2I/dV2 feature, so that a K/K′ imbalance can be told apart from a Γ-versus-K multiband gap? A region with different interlayer coupling in the same crystal would test the predicted t⊥ dependence.

You write that for the concave Hc2(T) "alternative explanations have also been proposed [63–66]" (p. 2); which of these did you compare with your data, and do the Hc2 fits constrain the ratio of the two gaps seen by STM?
